brief.scope: Independently review the three corrected Grok adapter test files against the merged declared mechanics and original review/ruling. No runtime inspection or edits. Verify all original defects closed: valid six-axis rebounds and stale witness refusals, independently held evidence, transport/insertion/resume identities, role-specific encoding, unconditional source isolation, closed results, environment/model controls and byte/token bounds. Reproduce 66/90 assertion-red with zero errors, exact hashes, registered lint and custody. Check compiler versus launch-side observation ownership; do not force capability grading into compile_launch. Contracts retain documentary follow-ups, so distinguish a test blocker from a known source-only residual. Return APPROVE/CHANGES with exact SHA and concrete oracles, no broad redesign. No full floor, vendor, settings or live state.

findings.claim: Every relative evidence handle resolves to a nonexistent path beneath the declared evidence root: root is <fixture>/evidence while the handle paths keep the 'evidence/' prefix, so the join doubles the component. Measured: root=/tmp/adapter-fixture-XXXX/evidence, verification rel=evidence/mock-verification.json, joined=/tmp/adapter-fixture-XXXX/evidence/evidence/mock-verification.json exists=False, while the bytes are planted at /tmp/adapter-fixture-XXXX/evidence/mock-verification.json. Same for witness.json and age-policy.json. dispatch/CONTRACT.md:348-350 requires every handle to resolve beneath held root and makes missing evidence unresolved, so an implementation that checks 'exact held evidence bytes/digests' (CONTRACT.md:367) refuses every case. All positive admissions become impossible, and the C5 replaced-bytes control at test_output_capability.py:647 then refuses whether or not the plant landed, so it discriminates nothing.
findings.reproduce: python3 -m unittest discover -s <record>/out -p 'test_probe_custody.py' (probe retained at out/test_probe_custody.py; it prints root, each relative handle, the joined path and its existence)

findings.claim: Externally built identities carry adapter.config_sha256 = digest_name('config'), but FixtureRoot.transport overwrites the descriptor's config_sha256 with config_digest(configuration, insertion, relay). Measured on the worker path: descriptor 40b3edcc1c2299abca137505affea122fa779ce27d27628e9fa72f7d5e8ed8e4 versus identity 9b800f619dafcdcb82df9451e2c51038033c131b0326a1e700a45f1cd43b58db (equal=False); the auto-built identity path is consistent (equal=True). harness-capabilities.md:339-349 requires descriptor adapter.config_sha256 to equal capability identity adapter.config_sha256 byte-for-byte, so every test_output_capability.py case that supplies its own identity presents stale evidence. Seven positive expectations cannot hold, and the five LeafEqualityRefusesBroaderProofs refusals fire on this mismatch rather than on their planted faults. test_descriptor_adapter_fields_must_equal_capability_identity is self-contradictory: :803 asserts success and :811 asserts cap['config_sha256'] == desc['config_sha256'], which the supplied identity makes unsatisfiable unless the compiler rewrites the field from the descriptor, defeating the check the test is named for.
findings.reproduce: python3 -m unittest discover -s <record>/out -p 'test_probe_config.py' (probe retained at out/test_probe_config.py; it prints all six descriptor-versus-identity rows for a supplied identity and for the auto-built one)

findings.claim: The vector carries two independent defects and pins an undeclared refusal-class priority. manifest['grammar'] is set to None (unmeasured grammar, harness-capabilities.md:241 -> unresolved) and manifest['adapter']['grammar_sha256'] is separately replaced, while the identity retains the real grammar digest, so the descriptor/identity mapping at harness-capabilities.md:345 is also broken (stale). Line 618 requires 'unresolved' in the line. This is the same class the ruling's PARTIAL forbade: a multi-defect case cannot fix validation order. Single-defect form: set the same 'unmeasured' digest on both the descriptor and the identity, leaving only the absent grammar.
findings.reproduce: Implement compile_launch to check descriptor-to-identity equality before grammar measurement: it returns 'output-capability: ... stale ...', assertIn('unresolved', line) at :618 fails, though the implementation is contract-conformant.

findings.claim: The conduct half of the descriptor-to-identity adapter mapping is untested. Both conduct adapter key constants are declared and never referenced by any test; the only mapping case is worker-only and asserts WORKER_ADAPTER_KEYS / WORKER_MANIFEST_ADAPTER_KEYS. harness-capabilities.md:339-350 declares six equality rows and states they cover both closed adapter objects completely, so adapter.normalizer_sha256 and the conduct six-field descriptor have no oracle at all.
findings.reproduce: grep -n 'CONDUCT_ADAPTER_KEYS\|CONDUCT_MANIFEST_ADAPTER_KEYS' ops/devlane/harness/tests/test_adapter_argv.py ops/devlane/harness/tests/test_output_capability.py -> no matches. Return a conduct capability whose adapter.normalizer_sha256 differs from the descriptor's: every test still passes.

findings.claim: The over-length case does not exercise the per-token byte bound. The token is 'x' * 257, which is undeclared vocabulary and not even flag-shaped, so a conforming implementation refuses it on the grammar match alone and never reaches the 256-byte check. Ruling item 6 (harness-capabilities.md:404) asks for per-token bounds exercised separately. The author's own p3 justification, that a closed grammar cannot declare a 257-byte name, is not established: harness-capabilities.md:211-216 bounds values to 1..128 bytes but sets no length limit on option names, and ats.flag_token(257) already produces the declared shape.
findings.reproduce: Implement match-declared-name-first, bounds-after: the 'x'*257 token refuses as unknown vocabulary at index 0 and the test passes with the byte bound never consulted; adding flag_token(257) to BYTE_BOUND_GRAMMAR would be the single-defect case.

findings.claim: The witness member of the evidence handle is never read or varied by any test. dispatch/CONTRACT.md:334-344 makes witness a required exact {path,sha256} handle resolved under the same custody as verification, and CONTRACT.md:348-350 requires held-byte and digest comparison for it too, but no case plants a mismatched witness digest, an unreadable witness or an absent one. The stale and unresolved arms all run through identity, selection or checked_at instead.
findings.reproduce: grep -n 'evidence.witness' ops/devlane/harness/tests/test_adapter_argv.py ops/devlane/harness/tests/test_output_capability.py -> no matches. Implement compile_launch ignoring transport.evidence.witness entirely: all 66 tests behave identically.

envelope.note:
Changes. The seven upheld findings from 20260906T125857Z-review-claude-10edd9 are closed and the receipts reproduce, but two custody defects introduced by the correction make most positive cases unpassable against a conforming implementation.

Measured here, at f125c9f7db8c8868763646baf55e0a97a0868ae0. Current sha256 equal the resealed record: adapter_test_support.py 095de81ebc65038f3252212a54ce38cb31c4619e98899533d7e3e876039e3a43, test_adapter_argv.py f718a3d63a9a3f1e2953415d4b33caaaaf855a00c1a6b17f78fedfbaa2df073b, test_output_capability.py 827da6dd167a993e0c9620995beddbac1527003c59e2f012a1a2f52ac341da68. Originals at d3ea314ba00456ed65751d3f9aa0381e000a58b0 reproduce as 7adb1c9b..., 977c7d84..., 2816833c... via git show | sha256sum. ops/devlane/harness/adapters.py is absent (ls ops/devlane/harness). Red receipt reproduced: test_adapter_argv.py Ran 40 tests, FAILED (failures=64); test_output_capability.py Ran 26 tests, FAILED (failures=26) — 66 tests, 90 assertion failures, 0 errors, every one on the MISSING_LAUNCH assertion, not on collection. ruff check on the three files: All checks passed. python3 ops/devlane/hooks/claude/test-guard.py on the three files: every plant is guarded (3 file(s) scanned). git diff --check 710dbac..f125c9f on the tests directory: clean. Working tree clean; I edited nothing in the snapshot, and both probes live in out/.

Closed, verified against the merged contracts. Role axis: six valid rebounds each get their own selection, grants and transport, measured holds only successful invariants, assertNotIn('refused', ...) at :277 pins that, and the stale conductor-witness and conflicting job_role refusals are separate tests. Worker encoding: WORKER_CAPABILITY_KEYS (9) and WORKER_ADAPTER_KEYS (4) match dispatch/CONTRACT.md:294-304 and :306-309 exactly; conduct keeps 11 and 5. Transport custody: TransportHandle exposes exactly the eight members of harness-capabilities.md:131-142 and EvidenceHandle exactly the nine of CONTRACT.md:334; config_digest hashes {configuration,insertion,relay} with relay.resume nulled, which is what makes the relay launch and resume invariants agree. Insertion: bounds asserted at :390-391, contiguous forwarding at :396-398, and the changed-index binding refusal at :400 works because the config digest binds both indices. Resume: retained session.id required in argv without freezing a flag spelling, expected resume vector compared, relay resume asserted equal to launch argv on the empty grammar. Source isolation: reads and denials are required kwargs of identity_for, and empty denials with empty outputs now refuse (:144), so discrimination no longer rests on output emptiness. Result: is_success itself requires set equality on the five keys. Controls: subprocess spy with a positive arm proving it fires, model containing 'write' unsubstituted, environment compared for full equality against the trusted map with PATH/HOME/TMPDIR canaries seeded and assertNotIn('TMPDIR', env), duplicate assertions gone. Bounds: 64/65 on a repeatable grammar and 8192/8193 (32x256 and 63x128+129) are single-defect, both refusing at index zero as the vector-level rule requires.

The two blockers are fixture-level and narrow. First, the evidence root and the relative handles disagree by one path component, so nothing resolves beneath root; either drop the 'evidence/' prefix from verification_rel, witness_rel and age_policy_rel, or move root — but root must stay outside the snapshot, out and scratch trees per CONTRACT.md:335-337, so the prefix is the side to change. Second, adapter_descriptor's placeholder config_sha256 survives on every identity the output-capability tests build for themselves, while transport() recomputes the descriptor's; the tests that let transport() build the identity are already consistent, so the fix is to compute the config digest once and hand it to both.

Compiler versus launch-side ownership reads correctly and I am not asking for a change there. test_independent_observation_of_a_forbidden_write_is_held_apart asserting success is right: CONTRACT.md:362-363 makes verification bytes opaque to the compiler and :382-383 puts the planted-forbidden-write proof at launch's evidence counterparty. The relabelled self-consistent neighbour is likewise correctly not a compile fault (CONTRACT.md:385-386). The author's six p3 residuals are source-side documentary follow-ups, not test blockers, and three of them (contract standing still PROPOSED, no declared in-process refusal exception type, synthetic relay fixture) belong to the contract owner; I have not counted them again.

Limits, declared. I did not read or write an implementation — there is none. I ran only the two focused suites and the two read-only probes in out/; no full floor, no vendor, settings or live state, no runtime inspection of an installed harness. Standing consequence, not a new finding: ops/bin/suites.sh:17 discovers ops/devlane/harness/tests, so the lane's single green oracle is red by 90 failures on this branch until adapters.py lands, and under AGENTS.md the PR stays draft until then.
